assumptions: Leakage analysis assumes target is the prediction label; the deployment population and prediction timestamp were not specified.
The standard conversion 1 tonne = 1000 kg is assumed for unit harmonization.
Exact repetition of every field including row_id 5 is treated as a probable duplicate-export error, subject to source-owner confirmation.
row_id is treated as an identifier, not a predictive feature; its missing value 6 is not by itself evidence of a missing record.

baseline.description: Training-fold mean predictor after excluding target_copy, future_score, and row_id, using entity-disjoint folds and fold-local preprocessing.
evidence: This is the simplest leakage-safe predictive baseline for a numeric target.
No baseline metric was run because the deployment target, evaluation metric, category mapping, and disposition of the negative-mass record remain unresolved.

candidate_models: Mean-only baseline: lowest implementation cost and a variance reference; falsified as useful if a leakage-safe candidate cannot improve a predeclared metric across entity-held-out folds.

Regularized linear model with fold-local one-hot encoding, standardized numeric fields, missing/sentinel indicators, and no leaked fields: low cost and interpretable; unsuitable if residual checks show stable nonlinear structure or interactions.

Shallow tree ensemble with the same allowed inputs and fold-local preprocessing: moderate cost and nonlinear fit; rejected for current selection because 10 unique rows make variance and overfit risk dominant; reconsider only with materially more independent entities.

Global date-blocked model was considered as a split/modeling workflow but rejected for the default design because repeated entities can cross the boundary and deployment to known versus unseen entities is unspecified.
claims: All numeric counts, equality relationships, fold memberships, hashes, and schema conformance reported as verified were produced by local commands in this run.
The 250 kg value is classified as plausible because the local dictionary permits values up to 300 kg.
The value 99 is classified as a sentinel because the local dictionary explicitly defines it as such.
No predictive performance, human approval, correction, or model selection is claimed.
code_artifacts: No persistent code artifact was created; audits and split sanity checks were executed as inline Python 3 scripts.

wc -l case/input/data.csv and sed -n on both listed case inputs
sha256sum on both inputs; git status --short; attempted inline python audit (failed because python was not installed)

inline python3 deterministic entity-fold sanity test, followed by sha256sum and git status --short
inline Python 3 validation of the returned observation against observation.schema.json
data_findings: Verified: the CSV parses as 11 data rows and 10 columns.
Probable error: CSV lines 6 and 7 are byte-equivalent records with row_id 5; exact deduplication leaves 10 records. Preserve both raw rows and record any deduplication as a reversible decision.
Definite domain violation requiring correction or quarantine: row_id 4 has mass_value -5 kg; mass amount cannot be negative under the supplied shipment interpretation.
Missingness: row_id 3 has the only blank feature value (1/11 rows).

Known sentinel, not a plausible numeric extreme: row_id 8 has feature 99, which the dictionary identifies as a device-mode sentinel. Retain a sentinel indicator and exclude 99 from numeric fitting/imputation.
Plausible extreme, not an error: row_id 9 has mass_value 250 kg; the dictionary explicitly permits bulk shipments up to 300 kg.
Valid mixed-unit value: row_id 3 has 0.012 tonne, equivalent to 12 kg; the other ten rows use kg.
Category encoding is inconsistent: red/Red/R and blue/BLUE occur. Case-only normalization is supported; mapping R to red is plausible but unverified and requires a codebook or human decision.
Direct leakage: target_copy equals target in all 11 rows.
Temporal leakage: future_score - target equals 1 in all 11 rows, and the dictionary says future_score is recorded one day later.

Storage order is not chronological within entity A: 2026-01-03 precedes 2026-01-02 in the file. Sort by parsed date within entity before any temporal procedure; file order itself is not a data-value error.
The row_id sequence skips 6, but identifier contiguity is undocumented, so this is an audit flag rather than a verified error.
experiment_design: Default proposal for unseen-entity generalization: exact-deduplicate using all non-split-derived raw fields, then deterministic three-fold entity holdout with tested folds {A,D}, {B,E}, and {C,F}.
Within each fold, fit category encoding, imputation, scaling, and the estimator on training rows only; apply frozen transformations to held-out rows.
Exclude future_score and target_copy at schema level before splitting; exclude row_id and raw entity from predictors while retaining them for provenance/grouping.
Compare the training-mean baseline, regularized linear model, and only if more independent entities become available, a shallow tree ensemble using a predeclared metric.

If deployment instead predicts future observations of already-known entities, replace the default with per-entity forward chaining after confirming the estimand; do not report the two designs as interchangeable.
falsification_tests: Duplicate hypothesis: falsified if source transaction identifiers show the two row_id 5 records are distinct legitimate events despite identical exported fields.
R-to-red mapping: falsified by an authoritative category codebook assigning R another meaning.
Unseen-entity split choice: falsified if the declared deployment objective is prediction of later records for already-observed entities.
Linear-model suitability: falsified if, on adequate additional entity-held-out data, a preregistered residual/nonlinearity check and metric consistently favor a nonlinear candidate.

Leakage exclusions: falsified only by evidence that either field is genuinely available and independent of target at the actual prediction timestamp; the supplied dictionary currently contradicts this.

constraints: Exclude future_score, target_copy, row_id, and raw entity identifier from predictors.
No entity may appear in both training and test portions of an entity-disjoint fold.
Deduplicate before assigning folds so duplicate records cannot cross a boundary.
Do not silently coerce negative mass, sentinel 99, missing feature, or unverified category aliases.
Raw inputs remain immutable; derived records carry provenance and decision status.
notes: Subtask flow: immutable raw rows -> audited derived rows -> leakage exclusions -> entity-disjoint split -> fold-local preprocessing -> baseline/candidate evaluation.
Evaluation metric and deployment estimand are unresolved, so model selection is blocked.

Audit log design is append-only with event_id, timestamp, actor, raw row reference/hash, field, old value, proposed value, reason/evidence, severity, status, and supersedes_event_id; reversals append a superseding event rather than overwriting history.
parameters: Unit factor: tonne to kg multiplier 1000.
Deterministic three-fold entity allocation tested: {A,D}, {B,E}, {C,F} as held-out groups.
Any imputation, scaling, encoding, or model hyperparameters must be learned on each training fold only.
units: mass_value is converted to kg in derived data only.
date is calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form.
feature and target units are not supplied.
variables: X_i = category, harmonized mass in kg, cleaned feature value, feature-missing indicator, and feature-sentinel indicator.
g_i = entity and t_i = parsed date.
d_i = reversible audit disposition: retain, quarantine, correct, deduplicate, or supersede.

human_gates: Source owner must confirm the row_id 5 duplicate disposition and the negative-mass correction or quarantine.
Data steward must approve the category codebook, especially whether R maps to red.
Problem owner must declare prediction timestamp, deployment population, evaluation metric, and acceptable threshold before model evaluation or selection.
Any audit decision must be appended with evidence and may only be changed by a superseding event.
reality_constraints: future_score is recorded one day after target and is unavailable at the target prediction time.
target_copy is derived from target and therefore cannot be a predictor.
Entities A, B, and C have repeated observations, so row-random splitting can place the same entity in train and test.
Only 11 rows (10 after exact deduplication) and six entities are present, so performance estimates would have high variance.
Preprocessing statistics and category mappings must be fitted or fixed without looking at held-out labels or held-out feature distributions.
